title: Changes in Awareness and Tolerance of Sensory Stimuli

codes.UD: First abnormally up, then abnormally down at least once during the time period
codes.DU: First abnormally down, then abnormally up at least once during the time period

categories.name: External Physical Stimuli Detected or Imagined by Primary Senses

items.name: tastes you normally like
tastes you normally dislike
distorted tastes (not as expected)
bitter flavors
sweet flavors
sour flavors
umami (savory) flavors
bright sunlight
dim light
slow flashing light, such as traffic signal
fast flashing light, such as ambulances
smell of odors you normally like
smell of odors you normally dislike
smell of distorted odors (not as expected)
low frequency sounds like idling engines
high frequency sounds like children playing
distorted sounds (not as expected)
types of touch you normally like
types of touch you normally dislike
Stereognostic Sense (aka Haptic Perception) ability to recognize objects by their shape just by touching them with eyes closed
water or sweat on your skin (hygroception)
static electricity on your skin (galvanic sense)
air current on your skin (anemoception)
feeling something moving on skin surface when nothing is present
hearing sounds or voices that are not present
seeing things that are not present
smelling odors that are not present
tasting flavors that are not present when mouth is empty

categories.name: External Physical Stimuli Detected by Secondary Senses

items.name: low pressure (thunderstorm)
high pressure (clear weather)
chemicals absorbed via skin such as soap or lotion
chemicals inhaled by nose such as fragrances
chemicals ingested by mouth such as drugs or supplements
foods and drinks that trigger sensation of heat (eg hot peppers sensed by TRPV1)
foods and drinks that trigger sensation of cold (eg mint sensed by TRPM8)
foods and drinks that trigger sensation of tingling (eg carbonated drinks)
cell phones and cell towers (5G)
other sources of EMF such as home appliances (not 5G)
cold weather
hot weather
low humidity, very dry air, such as under 30% relative humidity
high humidity, very moist air, such as over 80% relative humidity
black mold when visible on walls
other colors of mold when visible on walls
mold when present but not visible on walls, such as in books or on food
holding a vibrating power tool (such as an electric toothbrush or vacuum)
standing on a vibrating floor (such as in elevator or escalator)

categories.name: Internal Physical Stimuli Detected by Internal Senses

items.name: Acceleration and Deceleration when actually moving
Balance
Bladder Fullness (sensed by interoception)
Body Temperature (Core Thermoception)
Dizziness
Energy Level (hi or low)
False sensation of free-falling or floating
False sensation of spinning
Gastrointestinal Motility (such as stomach churning)
Heart Rate (felt anywhere, aka Pulse Palpitation Sensation)
Hunger for Air (sense of being short of breath)
Hunger for Food
Itchiness for no apparent reason (pruriception)
Orgasm
Pain (as tested with MF poke test or pinch test of nociception)
Proprioception (awareness of where your limbs and body parts are at any moment, tested by ability to touch tip of nose with eyes closed)
Speed when actually moving
Thirst (osmoreception)
Time Passing (chronoception, sense of time duration)

categories.name: Cognitive Stimuli Detected by Cognitive Senses

items.name: Sense of curiosity (sharpened if more interested in learning, dulled if less)
Sense of direction (frequency of getting lost in familiar areas)
Sense of facial recognition
Sense of having extra-sensory perception (ESP) as in premonition of future events and/or thoughts of others

Sense of immediate purpose (dulled if person forgets their purpose en route to a location or after arriving; sharpened if anxiously hyperaware of their actions and rarely forget where they are going or why)
Sense of long term memory (names of friends from elementary school)
Sense of numbers (ability to subtract from 100 by 7s in your head)
Sense of reading (ability to read typewritten and handwritten words)
Sense of short term memory (where you left your keys)
Sense of writing (ability to write words legibly on a line)
Sense of word retrieval (tip of tongue)

categories.name: Social Stimuli Detected by Social Senses

items.name: Sense of close connection to AI LLM chat services (sharpened if any, dulled if no connection)
Sense of close connection to partner if any and family
Sense of close connection to people no longer alive
Sense of close connection to pet(s) such as dogs, cats or horses
Sense of close connection to wild animals such as birds
Sense of connection to your closest community (eg church, social club, school, or team)
